title: Cluster Attach Journey Map and Quick-Fix Palette
creator: Asha Kapoor
project: Private Console UX: Network & Cluster Operability
description: Design a compact, actionable journey map for attaching a tenant to a private cluster and a contextual quick-fix palette for common connectivity and upgrade problems. Focus on reducing mean time to resolution for operators by surfacing targeted remediation actions, linking to runbooks, and providing safe defaults for canary rollouts and egress policies.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive journey map shows step-by-step attach flow from onboarding to health validation
Quick-fix palette presents 3 contextual suggestions for connection failures with one-click suggested actions
Design includes fail-safe confirmations and a clear audit comment input for Private/VPC actions
Figma prototype demonstrates desktop interactions and compact mobile-friendly fallback
Handoff spec includes states for success, transient failure, permanent failure, and rollback suggestion
comments: 2025-03-12 - Asha Kapoor: Initial ticket created after workshop with ENG and PM. Goals: reduce operator decision time when a tenant attach fails due to networking or upgrade drift.

2025-03-13 - Liam O'Connor (Engineering): Noted that KV cache priming can cause attach latency spikes; recommend calling out cache warmup step in the map and offering a 'pre-warm' action in quick-fix palette.

2025-03-14 - Priya Menon (Product): Prioritize egress policy validation and clear error messaging for blocked ports. PM requests an extra confirmation for any action that modifies customer routing tables.

2025-03-15 - Marco Alvarez (Design/Assignee): Prototype v0.1 uploaded to Figma. Included small palette with three suggested actions: re-run attach (idempotent), toggle ephemeral routing (safe), and open diagnostic trace (read-only). Calling out audit text box requirement.
2025-03-16 - Security Review (note): Security flagged the quick-toggle for ephemeral routing; need to gate behind RBAC and log HSM-enforced key usage. See attached runbook draft.

2025-03-17 - Usability Feedback (Eng + PM): Engineers suggested adding estimated time-to-resolution and confidence score to each palette action. PM asked for a collapsed/expanded view to avoid clutter for smaller screens.

2025-03-18 - Marco Alvarez: Updated prototype to include confidence badges and an inline preview of the audit entry. Preparing handoff spec and component states for the next design review on 2025-03-20.
decisions: Keep quick-fix palette limited to maximum 3 actions to minimize decision fatigue
All palette actions require audit comment and are gated by RBAC; ephemeral routing toggle exposed only if user has 'network-admin' role
Show estimated impact and confidence metadata for each suggested action based on past telemetry
Provide an explicit fallback button 'Open Support Runbook' that links to read-only runbook for non-privileged users
next_steps: Finalize component states and motion specs in Figma (Marco) - due 2025-03-20
Engineering feasibility review for pre-warm cache action and required telemetry hooks (Liam) - due 2025-03-22
